title: Garden Kneelers and Flip-Over Kneeler Seats: A Pad Versus a Bench
subtitle: A simple foam pad cushions your knees, while a kneeler bench adds a seat, so here is how to compare the two and what to check before you buy.
excerpt: A foam kneeling pad, like the Fiskars at $7.75 (Home Depot, November 2026), cushions your knees. Kneeler benches cost more and add a seat. Here is how to compare them.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: For many gardeners, the hardest part of weeding isn't the weeds. It's getting down to them, staying there in comfort, and getting back up again. Bare knees on hard soil or a stone path can start to ache quickly.

Two simple tools can help. A kneeling pad is a cushion you put under your knees. A kneeler bench is a low frame with a padded seat, and some, though not all, flip over to switch between kneeling and sitting. The pad costs a few dollars. The benches cost a good deal more. Which one makes sense depends on what is hardest for you.
How They Work, and What Each Can and Cannot Do

A kneeling pad is a flat cushion. You drop it on the ground, kneel on it, and move it along as you work. It is light, cheap and easy to store. What it cannot do is help you get up. It has no seat and no handles to push up on, so you still rise from the ground under your own power.

A kneeler bench is a padded seat on a sturdy frame, handy for tending a low bed or taking a break. Designs differ. The Gardener's Supply kneeler is described by the seller as flipping to become a padded gardening seat, while the Garrett Wade bench is listed as a portable bench and kneeler with a soft foam seat. The notes do not say whether it flips, and neither page confirms handles, so check each product page for how it works and whether it has handles.

Be realistic about the limits. A kneeler seat can help with getting down and up, but it does not remove the strain of bending or digging. Some people find raised beds or long-handled tools suit them better. A steel bench is also heavier than a foam pad, which matters if carrying or folding things is already a struggle.

items: Weight capacity: benches list a maximum load. Garrett Wade lists 330 lbs and Gardener's Supply lists 250 lbs, so check the number against the person using it.
Seat height and kneeling clearance: where a page lists them, check that they suit you. Garrett Wade gives a 17.5-inch seat height and 4 inches of kneeling clearance.
Handles: if handles matter to you, confirm on the product page that the bench has them and that they look sturdy.
Weight and folding: think about who will carry it from the shed and whether they can fold it easily.
Returns and warranty: check the return window and any warranty before you buy. Garrett Wade lists a 90-day guarantee with free returns, and Fiskars lists a full lifetime warranty.
Shipping: costs vary. Gardener's Supply banners free shipping on orders over $199.
Sales: promotions, like Garrett Wade's code, are short-lived, so check the current price.

sections.content: Set a bench on level, firm ground before you put weight on it. Check the weight capacity first, and read the maker's instructions for how to use and fold it.
Take short breaks. If your bench has a seat side, it can give you a quick rest, and a tool caddy, like the nylon one that comes with the Garrett Wade bench, keeps small tools within reach.
A kneeler is a gardening aid, not a medical device. If you have serious knee, hip or balance problems, ask your doctor or clinician whether kneeling is right for you before you buy.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: If sore knees are your only complaint, a low-cost pad may be all you need. If getting up off the ground is the hard part, a bench may be worth a look, once you have checked its details on the product page. Happy planting.

products.name: Fiskars 11 in. x 18 in. Kneeling Cushion (model 394210-1002)
products.blurb: Suits gardeners who mainly want to protect their knees and can get up without help. It is a flat lattice-pattern pad with a full lifetime warranty, but it has no seat and no handles.

products.name: Portable Bench & Kneeler (SKU 12A04.03)
products.blurb: A good fit for someone who wants a soft foam seat 17.5 inches off the ground, with 4 inches of kneeling clearance. It has a steel frame rated to 330 lbs, an included nylon tool caddy, and a 90-day guarantee with free returns.

products.name: Deep Seat Garden Kneeler (item 40-009)
products.blurb: For gardeners who want a kneeler that flips into a padded seat and has sides that fold in for storage. It holds up to 250 lbs; the seller does not list dimensions or seat height, so confirm those before ordering.
